newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 1.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
WALLDORF- Ad agency Silbermann wins the "customer care" account from Daimler-Benz. The company plans to use the account to train 3,300 car dealers in better customer service. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - TUI travel company awards its ad account to Menzel, Nolte and Heinemann, leaving Springer & Jacoby. (Horizont)
DUESSELDORF - Trendy clothier S. Oliver invests 12 million marks ($6.5 million) in advertising its brand name on the uniforms of the Borussia Dortmund (BVB 09) soccer team. (Die Welt)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Marketing products on the Internet is carving a larger niche in the German market and is the most important new trend in direct marketing, an industry expert says. The director of interactive media at the German Direct Marketing Association (DDV), Monika Beumers, says marketing in cyberspace has become a window of opportunity, particularly for mid-sized companies.
(Reuter)

MUNICH - Publisher Burda foresees continued growth with development of new magazine projects. Burda plans to bring more than 10 new magazines to the market this year, which it says should lead to boosts in sales and profits. Burda is the second largest publisher in Germany. (Reuter)
BONN - Private stations want to continue to discuss expanding access to the cable network with Deutsche Telekom, the private broadcasters association (VPRT). (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - German industrial conglomerate Daimler-Benz AG says earnings from its stake in the Airbus Industrie commercial airliner consortium totalled 173 million marks in the first half of this year, up from 132 million a year earlier. A Daimler spokesman says the earnings represented its full share of the Airbus consortium's profits but said the figure can fluctuate strongly due to order flows and be misleading. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Two Bavarian banks which plan to merge to form a new German banking giant say they are sure shareholders will accept the share swap crucial to the deal and deny they got preferential tax treatment. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - The German government details the five-billion-mark privatisation of Bonn's remaining stake in the airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG aimed at keeping a majority stake in German hands.
(Reuter)
STUTTGART - Stuttgart prosecutors say they will quit their investigation into alleged insider trading by Daimler-Benz AG management board chairman Eckhard Cordes on condition he paid a fine. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Car rental firm Sixt AG says it plans, along with a Nuernberg-based insurance group, to acquire a majority stake in the Ford dealer MOHAG. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Thomas Giuliani will rejoin BMW this year as marketing director of the company's BMW Motorsport Limited unit. Giuliani is currently with Audi. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Ingo Retzmann will take over responsibility for marketing services at Rank Xerox. He was previously product manager for document production systems. (Horizont)

WALLDORF - Martin Rasch joins the board of directors at local TV staion tv.muenchen (tv.munich) and will also serve as sales director at its national marketing agency SVG Vermarktungsgesellschaft mbH. (Kress)
